LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to write neatly and legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to Learn: The learner learns independently as they identify good handwriting and use it to write neatly and legibly.

Values:
Responsibility: self –drive as the learner writes legibly and neatly.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learner Support Programmes: peer education as the learner demonstrates good handwriting to peers.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Good handwriting is emphasised in all the learning activities

Suggested Learning Resources

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as Hearing aids and amplifiers, charts showing words with the target letter sounds, flash

cards showing words with target letter sound, signed audio-visual recordings, print or digital stories, pocket charts, print and digital flash cards
